analyst_view.overall: Early view: this is a relegation six-pointer between two struggling sides. Promoted Maritimo, under Mitchell van der Gaag, had gone eight league rounds without a win after losing 0-2 at home to Santa Clara on 1 November. Rio Ave replaced Sotiris Silaidopoulos with Vasco Seabra in early October; he won his debut 3-2 against Nacional, but the results since have mostly been defeats.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. I lean lower: both teams are low on confidence, and in a game this important to the relegation fight neither is likely to take many risks. Maritimo have also been wasteful, with Mons Bassouamina missing two good chances against Santa Clara.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.3 corners. Maritimo at home should push more, while Seabra wants Rio Ave to keep the ball. Nothing in the news moves this away from the model.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I lean higher: a relegation fight between two sides on poor runs tends to be tense and stop-start, and the home crowd in Funchal will be demanding a result. The referee is not known yet, so this will be checked again nearer kick-off.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.5 shots. Maritimo create chances at home but convert few, and Rio Ave's games under Seabra have been fairly open, starting with the 3-2 against Nacional. I see no clear reason to move away from the model.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target, which looks high for two of the league's weaker attacks. Maritimo's finishing has let them down during their winless run, and a nervy game usually means more blocked and off-target shots. I lean a little lower.
